reference_bible_note: Local, self-contained copy. Deep brand voice, full cast bios (bible/CAST.md, bible/CHARACTER_BIBLE.md), bible/COMPLIANCE_GATE.md, bible/VISUAL_STYLE_CONTRACT.md, bible/CINEMATOGRAPHY_CONTRACT.md, bible/assets/, bible/characters/. This channel.json carries only what tools/preflight.py and the stage contracts need to run.

channel.name: Signed Anyway
channel.spine: A hidden financial decision destroys trust; both sides argue the case and the viewer decides who crossed the line.
channel.tagline: They knew the cost. They signed anyway.

models.image_note: Two distinct jobs. 04b/04c produce reference SHEETS (identity locks, a handful per episode, reused). 04f2 produces frame-0 STILLS — one per clip, the literal first frame each clip is conditioned on.
models.video_note: i2v, native prose, native audio. The generation unit is the clip: one approved frame-0 still conditions exactly one generation.

cast.reference_workflow: Per-episode, ONE six-panel sheet per character. NO persistent bare-figure masters; NOT clover's three-tier model. Deliverable per character = a single clean six-panel character sheet (front / 3-quarter / profile / full-body / emotional-range / full figure), generated from that character's bible/characters/CAST-XX.md prompt with the painterly style clause VERBATIM, plus the episode's wardrobe/condition overlay from story/characters.md. That sheet is the SOLE reference for every 04f2 frame-0 still — no separate portrait/full-body/seated deliverable (they are only a generation fallback if the sheet's face drifts). 'Never condition on a sheet' was a FLUX text-label/restyle failure and is formally overturned for this use (carried from sibling-repo, owner-flagged 2026-10-29). Try the sheet prompt direct first; portrait-first only on drift. Owner decisions 2026-10-29.
cast.locked_references_note: Channel-level source of truth for a cast identity, reused across episodes (see that folder's README). A character is promoted here on its SECOND use across episodes. Currently locked: CAST-001 Evelyn Shaw, CAST-010 Omar Haddad (both copied verbatim from the sibling repo sibling-repo's approved painterly signed-anyway assets — same channel, same cards v1.0.0, model-agnostic images). An 04b run copies from here, never regenerates a locked identity.
cast.episode_local_rule: A character absent from the CAST-001..010 registry that RECURS is promoted to its own CAST-XX-style card (owner sign-off). A character appearing in one episode only is episode-local: a scoped card at episodes/<EPID>/story/characters/ following the CAST-XX structure but marked episode-local. Owner direction 2026-10-29.
cast.flow_project_note: Owner-supplied 2026-10-29 for EP001 04b onward. All signed-anyway Muse Image / muse-image CLI runs target this project.

render.prompt_format_note: Owner-locked PromptRelay-style beat packet, adopted 2026-10-29 from the vidgen-codex-ltx sibling where a 20-second LTX-2.5 render of the beat form outperformed the regular-prose alternative. Every clip prompt in prompts/7-video-prompts.md is one 'GLOBAL:: Continue from the still. … Low motion.' line plus 'BEAT:: <frames> ::' lines totalling 481 (24fps x 20s + 1). The frame labels are a model-facing pacing convention passed through the current LTX-2.5 graph unchanged, NOT the old ComfyUI-PromptRelay node. Enforced by LTXV-D001/D002; see pipeline/LTX_I2V_CONTRACT.md.
render.generation_unit_note: One approved frame-0 still conditions exactly one 20-second clip. A dramatic scene from story/script.md becomes several clips, bridged in post with controlled inserts, room tone and J/L cuts — the bible's CINEMATOGRAPHY_CONTRACT discipline of 'do not generate a continuous ten-minute scene' still holds; only the unit length changed.
render.clip_duration_note: Fixed 20s for every clip, owner decision 2026-10-29. The bible's performance unit was updated to match, so nothing in this repo now states a different figure. At 24 fps this lands on 481 frames (1 + 8*60), satisfying num_frames%8==1; vidgen-dist takes SECONDS and derives the frame count itself, so never hand-enter a frame count. Watch at 04h whether performances pad or drift in the final third: 20s is longer than this channel's dramatic register was originally written for.
render.spoken_word_band_note: At this channel's 145 wpm a 20s clip carries ~32-36 quoted words if speech fills ~70% of the clip. UNVERIFIED on LTX-2.5 and derived, not measured — see research section 6, open question 2, and re-derive from the pilot batch.
render.style_echo: Cinematic painterly graphic-novel realism, restrained ink-navy and slate palette with aged-brass accents, matte prestige-drama lighting
render.style_echo_note: Updated 2026-10-29 to carry the painterly-graphic-novel medium (render.look_and_feel) plus tone/palette in one trailing phrase. This exact string is the closing sentence of every LTX clip prompt and is what LTXV-D041 excludes from the final-beat check — keep prompt and channel.json identical. The earlier grounded-corporate-drama phrasing did not name the medium and would have rendered photoreal.
render.look_and_feel: Cinematic painterly graphic-novel realism — the channel scope, for stills AND video. Hand-painted editorial texture with controlled visible brushwork; natural adult proportions and grounded facial anatomy (NOT caricature, NOT cel-shaded cartoon, NOT flat vector, NOT glossy 3D); restrained near-monochrome ink-navy and slate palette with aged-brass the only warm accent; soft directional prestige-drama (Rembrandt) key light, matte finish, deep-but-not-crushed shadow. Explicitly NOT photoreal. Faces read clearly at a 98-pixel crop. Inline this whole clause into every Muse Image image prompt and every LTX clip prompt's style anchor.
render.look_and_feel_note: Owner-confirmed 2026-10-29 with a style reference image. An earlier same-day note reinterpreting the look toward photoreal was WRONG and is withdrawn. bible/VISUAL_STYLE_CONTRACT.md and KEY_CHARACTER_PROMPTS.md §1 are correct as written — use their style anchor verbatim; do NOT swap it for a photoreal clause. style_echo below describes tone/lighting/palette, not the rendering medium. Open pilot-QA item (04h): whether LTX-2.5 holds this painterly look across a 20s i2v clip from a painterly still — untested, but it is the look; if it cannot, the fix is prompt/still craft, not switching to photoreal without a new owner decision.
render.on_screen_text: Native on-screen text is permitted (owner decision 2026-10-29). Muse Image renders short legible text reliably on frame-0 stills — prop labels, form fields, hand-inked initials, a document header — so readable prop text is baked into the 04f2 STILL and carried forward; the LTX clip prompt does not request new or changed text, so LTXV-D012 still stands for clip prompts. Exact critical figures that must be byte-identical across many shots plus the evidence graphics and the verdict card are still built in post — a consistency choice, not a capability limit.
render.negative_prompt_note_2: Reworked 2026-10-29 for the painterly-graphic-novel lock. Dropped 'cartoon', 'illustration', 'stylised rendering' — they fought the intended look. The list now suppresses what the painterly realism lock excludes (cel-shaded cartoon, caricature, flat vector, children's-book illustration, glossy 3D toy render) AND pushes the LTX render off its default photoreal (photorealistic photograph, DSLR photo), plus the unchanged safety/brand terms.
render.cfg_note: Render-validated on EP001 (2026-10-29), replacing the untested 1.0 default. At cfg 1.5 (SC01-SC12's original render) the base pass produced visible extra smoke off the practical table lamp in the hearing-room clips; owner judged those 12 acceptable as-is (the artifact was minor and lamp-localised) but dropped the setting for the remaining clips. 1.2 (SC13-SC29) rendered clean. Grade [B].
render.img_compression_note: Raised from the untested default of 18 on EP001 (2026-10-29) — a deliberate tightening of the anti-invented-motion/anti-invented-character lever (LTXVPreprocess), giving the model less freedom to add unrequested movement to a still. Applied to the full 29-clip batch, no adverse effect observed. Grade [B], confirms the lever still behaves as documented on LTX-2.5 (see research doc open question 4).
render.max_prompt_words_note: RUNAWAY TRIPWIRE, not a ceiling (retired 2026-10-29). LTX-2.5 has no vendor word limit and the Gemma encoder is built for long prompts; the old 200 figure was LTX-2-era sibling guidance. LTXV-D004 warns past 450 to catch a repeated room inventory or duration filler only. Never trim a load-bearing identity, audio or camera anchor to fit. See pipeline/LTX_I2V_CONTRACT.md §Length.
render.negative_prompt_note: Appended to pipeline/negative-prompt-base.txt at 04g, plus a 'second <Name>' term per cast member in the episode. This is the ONLY place suppression lives: the same terms in a positive prompt cause the artifact they name (LTXV-D010 rejects them).
